item.title: Claude Opus 5
item.description: Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic’s top-tier model, tuned specifically for agentic coding — multi-file features, large refactors, and end-to-end implementation work rather than single-shot completions. Give it a full task specification up front and it tends to run the whole way to a finished result instead of leaving stubs behind.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5
item.description: Claude Sonnet 5 closes most of the gap to Opus-tier quality on coding and agentic tasks while staying meaningfully cheaper — a solid default for the coding work that makes up most of a normal week, not just the hardest 20%.

item.title: Grok 4.6
item.description:
Grok 4.6 is xAI’s frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, and the current flagship behind Grok Build — xAI’s dedicated coding agent and terminal UI.

Why it stands out

  • Aggressive tiered pricing — a lower rate below 200K prompt tokens and a scaled-up rate above it, so short-context coding sessions stay cheap.
  • Grok Build, xAI’s open-source coding agent and TUI, gives it a purpose-built harness rather than relying only on third-party tools.
  • 500K-token context window, comfortably large for most real-world coding sessions.

Good for

Fast, iterative agentic coding workflows — especially teams already using Grok Build or wanting a cheaper alternative to the largest frontier models for everyday agent loops.

item.title: Kimi K2.7 Code
item.description:
Kimi K2.7 Code is Moonshot AI’s coding-focused release in the Kimi K2 line, built to carry end-to-end programming tasks across long, multi-turn agent sessions rather than one-shot completions.

Why it stands out

  • Always-on thinking mode that preserves full reasoning content across multi-turn conversations, instead of resetting context between steps.
  • Native multimodal mixture-of-experts architecture, accepting text and image input in the same coding session.
  • Frontier-competitive coding benchmarks at a fraction of the per-token cost of comparable Western frontier models.
  • Steep cache discount (roughly 80% off cache-miss input pricing), which rewards long, iterative agent loops that keep re-reading the same context.

Good for

Teams running long, agentic coding sessions who want frontier-adjacent reasoning quality without frontier-model pricing.

item.title: GLM-5.2
item.description:
GLM-5.2 is Z.ai’s (formerly Zhipu AI) flagship open-weight model — a 753-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts design released under the MIT license, with a 1M-token context window and full downloadable weights.

Why it stands out

  • MIT-licensed, 753B-parameter MoE weights, fully self-hostable with no usage restrictions.
  • 1M-token context window with up to 131K tokens of output in a single response.
  • Beats GPT-5.5 on FrontierSWE at roughly a sixth of the cost, per Zhipu’s own benchmarking.
  • Selectable High/Max reasoning modes, letting you trade latency for depth on harder multi-step coding tasks.

Good for

Teams that want a genuinely open, frontier-tier coding model to self-host, fine-tune, or run at scale without per-token lock-in.
